method_summary: Time-sampling ablation of round-01: retain 128 teacher targets, three proposals per original label, stable lower-median LPIPS-distance selection, reuse=1 and uniform weights. Replace the inference-anchored pair (0.1u, 0.1+0.9(1-u)) with complementary half-interval times (0.5u, 1-0.5u), randomly oriented within each pair. All tensors and random draws remain on CPU. All TeacherConfig fields are identical to round-01.

limitations_applied: The only completed own-track public FID is the round-01 joint method. There is no completed paired published-initialization baseline in these records.

prior_evidence_review.reason_for_choice: Follow the time-ablation direction recorded in our own round-01 analysis, holding teacher selection and all teacher parameters fixed. This produces an identifiable comparison of time-sampling methods at the same low target-generation and training cost, rather than adding another untested selection or weighting mechanism.
prior_evidence_review.previous_cli_timeout_preserved: The round-01 client used --wait-seconds 5 and exited with TimeoutError after ACCEPTED. A later same-job public terminal receipt is SUCCESS. Both the failure log and terminal result remain unchanged.

causal_hypothesis: Unvalidated hypothesis: with only 128 visits from the official EMA initialization, allocating half the samples to prefix k=0 may reduce supervision of other prefix conditions. Complementary uniform time pairs give each micro-batch one early-half and one late-half condition, with nominal marginal P(k)=0.1 for each k=0..9, and may provide more balanced useful updates at the same cost. FID could worsen if inference-near k=0 emphasis is beneficial; no direction is established by CPU prechecks or the prior joint result.

algorithm_change.inference_limit: A later round-01/round-02 comparison tests the overall time-sampling algorithm. It cannot establish median selection effectiveness, or separately attribute any effect to the marginal time distribution and the numerical within-pair relation.
